summary: Lease-drain + gang-preemption causing sustained p99 degradation in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
During the 2026-03-12 morning window we observed sustained p99 latency degradation and a ~30% drop in overall throughput for a single dedicated pool serving Peregrine Labs. The pool reports repeated "lease-drain" events followed by short gang-preemption cycles that coincided with many small long-lived streams from an internal tenant.

Impact:
- Customer (Peregrine Labs) seeing p99 latency increase from ~1.2s to 4.5s for text-generation routes.
- End-user timeouts and elevated API error rates (5xx from sidecars while waiting for allocations).
- Business impact: reduced SLA headroom and customer throttling of production traffic.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool id: dp-04b3-us-east
- Region: us-east-1 (primary)
- Model: redwood/rt-medium-1.4b pinned v1.3
- Autoscaler policy: predictive with burst window enabled, configured target_util=0.7

Steps to reproduce / observed pattern:
1) During customer steady traffic, background tenant T201 begins a steady stream of ~100 simultaneous long connections sending short requests every 2s.
2) GPU allocator marks multiple slots as "lease-drain" to rebalance KV-cache anchors (observed at 10:12:06).
3) Shortly after, gang-preemption is invoked to satisfy the long-lived streams, evicting several batches and causing a short allocation stall.
4) Autoscaler interprets the transient drop in observed utilization as underutilization and initiates a shrink, followed by an immediate grow once main workloads spike, producing oscillatory capacity (10:12–10:22).
5) Resulting behavior: repeated slot churn, increased queueing, and p99 amplification lasting ~10 minutes in each cycle.

Logs / snippets:
- allocator logs (dp-04b3-us-east): "INFO lease-drain initiated: selector=kv-anchor, affected_slots=6"
- scheduler trace: "preempt: gang-preempt tenant=T201 reason=long_streams"
- autoscaler: "shrink trigger: observed_util=0.43 target=0.7 window=2m" then "grow trigger: observed_util=0.82"
- sidecar errors: "RPC timeout waiting for GPU allocation (deadline exceeded)"

Additional notes:
- No underlying host-level GPU driver errors detected. GPU memory and temperature metrics normal.
- NVLink saturation counters show brief spikes aligning with eviction windows.
- The tenant causing long connections is internal and not customer traffic; their traffic pattern is atypical (many small streams kept alive).

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should avoid oscillating on short-lived allocation fluctuations and scheduler should avoid preempting stable high-priority customer batches for many small low-priority streams.

Contact / SLA details:
- Customer contact: ops@peregrine.ai (primary), account exec: Jordan Kim
- Customer reported via support portal at 2026-03-12T10:30:22Z
comments: 2026-03-12 11:05 — Marcus Cheng: Initial triage: reproduced allocation churn in staging with synthetic long-stream load. Hypothesis: combination of lease-drain policy + preemption threshold too permissive for this pool. Will instrument extra telemetry.

2026-03-12 12:40 — SRE Oncall (Priya Rao): Observed NVLink microbursts; added temporary affinity rule to keep active customer batches on stable GPUs while we patch preemption logic. Patch request: gh.com/redwood/infra/pull/1487.

2026-03-13 09:10 — Support (Elena Morales): Customer applied temporary traffic shaping to reduce long-stream concurrency; reported partial improvement but still sees p99 spikes during peak. Requested ETA for permanent fix.
2026-03-14 07:55 — Marcus Cheng: Deployed autoscaler debounce patch (increase shrink debounce from 2m -> 6m) in dp-04b3-us-east canary. Monitoring for three windows of peak traffic before rolling.
investigation_notes: 1) Reproduced with internal loadgen: mixing many long-lived short requests with regular batched workloads causes allocator to mark slots for lease-drain due to KV anchor reshuffle. 2) Gang-preemption logic currently prioritizes minimizing request latency for the small streams at the cost of evicting batched workloads; priority scoring is too flat. 3) Autoscaler shrink sensitivity is reacting to transient utility dips caused by eviction-induced queueing. 4) No hardware faults; root cause is scheduling + autoscale sensitivity plus noisy internal tenant. Correlation: p99 spikes line up with preemption events in scheduler logs.
resolution_notes: Workarounds / short-term: 1) Applied temporary tenant rate-cap and lowered preemption priority for internal tenant T201 (completed 2026-03-12 13:20Z). 2) Pinned critical customer routes to a subset of GPUs with affinity to avoid eviction during burst windows. 3) Rolled autoscaler debounce and increased shrink threshold in canary (dp-04b3-us-east).\nPermanent mitigations planned: 1) Update scheduler preemption policy to include batch-penalty score and protect pinned production batch slots. 2) Add autoscaler hysteresis + trend analysis to ignore <5m dips caused by preemption waves. 3) Add tenant-level long-stream detection and auto-classification to apply lower-preemption weights.\nFollow-up: Schedule postmortem and add a Confluence runbook entry describing detection and immediate mitigations. Target rollout of scheduler change in 2 weeks (2026-03-28).
